transcript.text: Samsung WW90T534DAW keeps coming up with 4C after a couple of minutes. Drum is dry. Any ideas before I call someone out?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. 4C on your Samsung means: Water supply issue - little or no water entering (tap/pressure/inlet mesh/hose). From what you have described, the most likely cause is blocked inlet mesh / filter. Where the fill hose screws onto the back of the machine there's a small mesh filter that can block with grit or scale. Unscrew the hose at the machine end and look into the inlet. Was the mesh blocked (and is it clean now), or was it already clean?
I'll give that a go. Turning the tap off and unscrewing the hose now.

Next: Inspect and clean the inlet mesh/filter. Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the fill-hose mesh filter is" — A small mesh filter sits inside the fill-hose connector at the tap/valve end and catches grit. Turn the tap off, unscrew the hose and rinse the mesh. Typical layout — your machine may differ.]
Mesh filter is clogged with grey grit and bits of limescale. Cleaning it now, then I'll refit the hose and retry.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the fill hose or its tap connection. Check the fill hose where it screws onto the tap and onto the back of the machine — a loose fitting or a missing or perished washer is the usual cause. Were the connections loose (and are they tight now), already tight and dry, or is the hose split or bulging?
Cleaned the mesh and refitted the hose, and it's filling normally now with no 4C. No leaks at either connection, and the hose isn't split or kinked.
Good news, that has sorted it. If it happens again, start with the same check. Is there anything else I can help with?
